cover.headline: You get TII's own business for free, and CG Power at a 65% discount: BUY
cover.lead: Tube Investments of India (TII) is the Murugappa group's engineering company: India's largest precision-tube maker, the leader in auto chains, the BSA and Hercules cycle brands, and the owner of 56.29% of CG Power, 70.46% of Shanthi Gears and a portfolio of start-ups led by TI Clean Mobility (electric commercial vehicles). On 30-Sep-2026 TII's market value (₹45,969 cr) was 39% **below the market value of its CG Power shares alone** (₹75,724 cr). We value TII the way the street does, as a **sum of the parts**: its own business at 19x Sep-28E core EPS (its own pre-CG forward P/E, 20.8x, cut by the 9.4% auto-component de-rating), the listed stakes at market less a **34% holding-company discount** (TII's own median since Sep-2024, a judgement: the 2021-26 median is a premium; 65% today), and the unlisted ventures at cost. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}} (today's discount persists and TICMPL's equity is worth nothing).

arguments.h: The discount is the widest in TII's history
arguments.p: From 2021 to mid-2024 TII traded at or above the value of what it owns. Since then CG Power kept rising and TII fell: on our convention the discount on the listed stakes went from ~0% (Jun-2024) to 65% (Sep-2026). Our base case assumes only a return to the post-2024 median (34%, close to MOSL's 35%). Every 10% move in CG Power is ~₹269 a TII share at that discount.

arguments.h: The standalone business is a high-return compounder
arguments.p: Precision tubes, chains and cycles earned ₹715 cr of core profit in FY26 (before CG dividends) at a 44% pre-tax ROIC, and generated ₹826 cr of free cash flow. Q1FY27 volumes grew 17%; margins dipped on steel costs that contracts pass through with a 2-3 quarter lag. At 19x Sep-28E core EPS of ₹47.4 it is worth ₹900 a share.

arguments.h: The ventures are the reason for the discount
arguments.p: TII has put ~₹1,600 cr into TI Clean Mobility, TI Medical, 3xper and others since FY22, and the residual block lost ₹550 cr at EBITDA in FY26. TICMPL's revenue grew 77% in Q1FY27 and management says peak losses are behind it, but ₹500 cr more is committed. We value the ventures at cost (₹88 a share): they are not the case for the stock.

arguments.h: Why not more upside, and what could go wrong
arguments.p: TII's shareholders get CG Power's value only through a ~₹115 cr dividend; nothing forces the discount to close, and TII has never sold a CG share. CG Power itself trades at ~106x trailing earnings, so the stake's value can fall fast (at ₹650 a CG share our target falls by ~₹617). Street targets standing on 30-Sep-2026: median ₹3,255.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether steel-price recovery lifts standalone margins back towards 12%, and TICMPL's quarterly loss.
CG Power's share price and results: the stake is ~85% of TII's look-through value.
The second ₹250 cr tranche into TICMPL (planned for Q3FY27) and any update on an IPO or new outside capital.
Break-even of the first EV business (guided for FY27); 3xper's regulatory inspection (expected FY28); TI Medical's IV-cannula plant.
Any capital-return or restructuring step (higher dividend, buyback, CG Power share sale): none announced.

sections.title: A precision-engineering company that owns most of CG Power

blocks.p: Tube Investments of India (TII) is the Murugappa group's engineering company. It makes precision steel tubes and strips, automotive chains and car door frames, and bicycles, and it uses the cash from those businesses to build or buy new ones. Its biggest asset is not a factory but a stake: 56.29% of CG Power and Industrial Solutions, the motors, transformers and switchgear maker it took over in November 2020 and turned around. It also owns 70.46% of Shanthi Gears, and has started an electric commercial-vehicle business (TI Clean Mobility, brand Montra Electric), a medical-devices business (TI Medical), a contract drug-development and manufacturing business (3xper) and several smaller ventures.

blocks.p: Two things stand out. First, **the CG Power stake alone (₹3,912 a share) is worth 65% more than TII's whole market value**: the market gives TII's own ₹8,556 cr business, Shanthi Gears and the ventures a negative value, or applies a large discount to the stake. Second, TII's own business is good but ordinary in growth: revenue grew 7.6% a year in FY22-26, core profit ~9% a year in FY23-26, with a 12-13% EBITDA margin and a very high return on capital (pre-tax ROIC 44%).

blocks.p: The common thread is the Indian capital and vehicle cycle. In Q1FY27 TII's engineering volumes grew ~17% and management called demand "pretty good across segments" with exports up double digits; the risks it named were steel and fuel inflation, cell prices for EVs, the West Asia conflict and Hyundai's weak output. None of TII's businesses has pricing power over steel: tube and chain contracts reset to steel prices with a one-to-three-quarter lag, which is why margins dip when steel rises (Q4FY26-Q1FY27) and recover after.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the volume tailwind is real and visible in Q1FY27; the margin will follow once steel prices are passed through. But the stock's value depends far more on CG Power's price and on the discount the market applies to it than on TII's tube volumes.

sections.title: TII's own businesses: a high-return tube maker with a cycles drag

blocks.p: Engineering (precision tubes and strips) is the core: ₹5,612 cr of FY26 revenue and ₹689 cr of PBIT (12.3%). It grew 12% in FY26 and 21% in Q1FY27 on volumes (+17%), new tube and strip capacity in western India (tubes ~30% utilised in May-2026, the Nashik strip plant to be full by end-FY27 or mid-FY28) and exports. Metal formed products (chains, door frames, fine blanking, railway sections) is slower: revenue +2% in FY26 with a 10.1% margin, held back by unprofitable railway tenders, Hyundai's weak production and a western greenfield plant running six months late. Cycles finally makes money (PBIT ₹19 cr in FY26 after a ₹18 cr loss in FY24) and management wants ~2 more points of margin in FY27. "Others" holds industrial chains (Rombo, 50%+ exports in special-purpose chains), TMT bars, truck bodies, optics, CDMO and Orange Koi.

blocks.callout: **So what:** TII's own businesses earned ₹715 cr of core profit in FY26 (before dividends from CG Power and Shanthi Gears), with a pre-tax ROIC of 44%. That is an excellent return, but growth has been modest (core profit ~9% a year since FY23) and Q1FY27 shows how exposed margins are to steel. We forecast core profit of ₹723 cr / ₹863 cr / ₹971 cr for FY27-29E: flat this year as the steel lag unwinds, then ~13-19% growth.

sections.title: CG Power: the turnaround that made TII, now 85% of its look-through value

blocks.p: TII took control of CG Power in November 2020, when it was a near-bankrupt company. Under TII's management CG Power's consolidated revenue rose from ₹2,964 cr (FY21) to ₹12,418 cr (FY26) and EBITDA from ₹116 cr to ₹1,641 cr. On 30-Sep-2026 it was worth ~₹1,34,485 cr (₹854.20 a share, 105.8x trailing earnings against a five-year median of 83.5x). TII's 88.65 cr shares (56.29%) were worth ₹75,724 cr, ₹3,912 per TII share, against TII's own share price of ₹2,375.

blocks.p: For TII's shareholders CG Power matters in three ways. **Value:** the stake is ~77% of our look-through value before the discount. **Cash:** TII receives only CG's dividends (₹115 cr in FY24, ₹1.30 a share); CG keeps most of its cash for its own growth (switchgear, transformers, the CG Semi OSAT plant with Renesas and Stars Microelectronics). **Earnings:** CG is ~58% of the EBITDA of TII's profitable blocks (72% of the consolidated total after the ventures' losses), which is why TII's consolidated P/E is not a useful yardstick. CG Power is covered separately; in this report we take its market price as given and do not form our own view of its value.

sections.title: TI Clean Mobility and the new ventures: ~₹1,700 cr invested, ~₹550 cr a year of EBITDA losses

blocks.p: **TI Clean Mobility (TICMPL, brand Montra Electric)** has four businesses: electric 3-wheelers (passenger and cargo; ~6,700 billed in FY26, ~120 outlets), e-tractors (first billing in Q1FY27), electric small commercial vehicles (TIVOLT, Eviator; 27% market share in Q4FY26) and heavy electric trucks (IPLTech, Rhino; ~28% share of a ~300-trucks-a-year market). Revenue reached ₹239 cr in Q1FY27 (+77%), but the segment lost ₹147 cr (₹136 cr a year earlier). Management says peak quarterly losses are behind it, one business should break even in FY27 and two more in FY28.

blocks.p: How much of TICMPL TII will own after conversion depends on the IPO valuation (CFO, Q1FY27 call). We value TII's interest at its cost (₹1,000 cr) in the base case, at the March-2026 fair-value mark (₹1,576 cr) in the bull case, and in the bear case at minus the present value of the ₹500 cr TII has still promised (equity worth nothing). The **other ventures** are smaller: TI Medical (sutures, surgical devices; ~₹200 cr revenue, ~20% growth guided, an IV-cannula plant from Aug-Sep 2026), 3xper (CDMO and APIs; a 200 KL plant at Naidupeta commissioned, regulatory inspection expected in FY28), Kcaltech (aluminium HVAC tubes), Orange Koi (metal injection moulding) and TI Optics (camera lenses; "yet to make inroads").

blocks.callout: **So what:** together the residual block (EV plus new ventures, net of eliminations) lost ₹550 cr at EBITDA in FY26 and about ₹110 cr in Q1FY27. We assume losses narrow to ₹384 cr in FY28E and ₹266 cr in FY29E, slower than management's break-even talk. Every ₹100 cr of loss is ~₹5 a share a year of TII's earnings; in the valuation the ventures are only ~₹88 a share at cost.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** TII's standalone business has a narrow, real advantage (scale, approvals, high asset turns) that shows up in returns rather than in pricing power: steel costs pass straight through, and margins are capped at ~12-13%. The wider "moat" is the Murugappa team's record in buying and fixing businesses. That is valuable but cannot be underwritten forward; the EV, medical and CDMO ventures have to prove it again.

sections.title: Consolidated revenue doubled since FY22; profit for TII's shareholders halved since FY24

blocks.p: TII's consolidated revenue was ₹22,847 cr in FY26, almost double FY22's ₹12,447 cr (the first full year with CG Power). But only ₹8,556 cr of it is TII's own business; ₹12,418 cr is CG Power, of which TII owns 56%. So the consolidated numbers say more about CG Power than about TII. Profit attributable to TII's shareholders was ₹637 cr (₹32.9 a share) in FY26, against ₹1,201 cr (₹62.1) in FY24. Two things explain the fall. FY24 carried a one-off: CG Power's ~₹540 cr of exceptional gains in the Dec-2023 quarter. And the new ventures, mostly TI Clean Mobility's electric vehicles, went from a small loss to a large one: the residual block (consolidated less TII, CG Power and Shanthi Gears) lost ₹550 cr at EBITDA in FY26 against ₹99 cr in FY24, and none of that loss is shared with minorities.

blocks.callout: **So what:** do not judge TII on its consolidated P/E (73x trailing on 30-Sep-2026) or its 10% consolidated margin. About 85% of what TII owns is the market value of CG Power, which investors can buy directly. The questions that matter are (1) what TII's own businesses earn and are worth, (2) what discount the market puts on the CG Power stake, and (3) how much more cash the EV and other new ventures will absorb. The rest of this report is built around those three.

sections.title: A cash machine at the core; the cash goes into new ventures, not to shareholders

blocks.p: TII's own businesses need little capital and return a lot on it: pre-tax ROIC of 44-55% in FY22-26 (company definition), free cash flow of ₹2,412 cr over FY22-26 (₹826 cr in FY26, 100% of profit). Where did it go? Into new subsidiaries: TII's cost of its unlisted subsidiaries rose from ₹161 cr (Mar-2022) to ₹1,673 cr (Mar-2026), mostly TI Clean Mobility (₹1,000 cr), TI Medical (₹265 cr) and 3xper (₹285 cr). Shareholders received ₹3.50 a share every year (~₹68 cr, under 10% of profit). Another ₹250 cr goes into TICMPL in Q3FY27 and ~₹300 cr a year into other subsidiaries.

blocks.callout: **Capital allocation verdict:** the CG Power deal (2020) was one of the best capital-allocation decisions in Indian industry: TII's 88.65 cr CG shares cost ₹806 cr and were worth ~₹75,700 cr on 30-Sep-2026. The ventures since then (EV, medical devices, CDMO, optics, MIM) have absorbed ~₹1,600 cr and none earns its cost of capital yet. TII behaves like a venture holding company funded by a precision-tube business. That is the case for owning it if you trust the Murugappa team to repeat CG Power, and the reason for the discount if you do not.

blocks.p: **Against the street.** The only consensus we found (Trendlyne, 6 analysts, 20-Jul-2026, before Q1) expected FY27 revenue +10.2% and profit +16.7%. We are higher on both: revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|n1}}% (Q1 was already +17%) and attributable profit +{{F.patGrowth.0|n1}}%. The gap is about the size of FY26's one-offs (₹42 cr of exceptional charges after tax and an ₹18 cr fair-value loss on TICMPL's preference shares, which no longer arises after the Mar-2026 restatement): on a clean FY26 base of ~₹697 cr our FY27E growth is 15.9%, close to consensus. It rests on CG Power growing ~15% and the ventures' losses no longer widening. MOSL, the only broker with a post-Q1 note in our sources, forecasts ~7% a year standalone profit growth over FY26-28E; our core standalone profit grows 9.9% a year over the same period, flat in FY27E.

blocks.callout: **What the engine can and cannot show.** The model has no minority-interest line, so tax and minorities share one rate (62.5% / 58% / 55%, against 66% in FY26); the rate falls as the untaxed venture losses shrink relative to CG Power's taxed profit. Model cash and net worth are consolidated and include CG Power's cash, which TII's shareholders cannot reach except through dividends; the standalone balance sheet is in "Balance sheet & cash".

blocks.p: The street median of the notes standing on 30-Sep-2026 is ₹3,255; Trendlyne's pre-Q1 consensus target was ₹3,402. MOSL's method has moved in one direction: the standalone multiple fell from 30x (Aug-2025) to 24x (Feb-2026) to 15x (Aug-2026) and the holding-company discount rose from 30% to 35%, yet its target barely moved (₹3,515 -> ₹3,315 -> ₹3,379) because CG Power's price rose. In other words, the street's target for TII is mostly a target for CG Power less a discount. At MOSL's 35% discount, the CG Power and Shanthi Gears stakes alone are worth ~₹2,648 a TII share at 30-Sep-2026 closes.

blocks.h: What the bears and bulls argue

bullets: **Bear:** Holding-company structure: ~85% of look-through value is a listed stake that investors can buy directly; TII pays only ₹3.50 a share in dividends and keeps funding new ventures.

**Bear:** TICMPL: ₹1,000 cr invested by TII and ~₹1,780 cr by outside investors; still loss-making (EV segment loss ₹147 cr in Q1FY27); conversion terms of the investors' CCPS depend on a future IPO valuation.
**Bear:** Standalone growth is modest (revenue CAGR 7.6% FY22-26; core PAT CAGR ~9% FY23-26) and steel-price lags make margins lumpy.
**Bear:** the stake is "trapped": TII has never sold CG Power shares, so TII's shareholders get CG Power's value only through a small dividend or a future restructuring that has not been announced.
**Bull:** the discount on 30-Sep-2026 (~65% on our convention) is the widest in TII's history; even a return to the post-2024 median closes a large part of the gap.
**Bull:** the standalone business is a 44%-ROIC compounder in its own right, and TICMPL has outside investors who valued their stake at ₹2,405 cr in Mar-2026.

sections.title: Valuation: TII's own business at 19x, CG Power at market less a 34% discount, gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}

blocks.p: TII is valued as a **sum of the parts (SOTP)**: its own businesses on a P/E multiple, CG Power and Shanthi Gears at their market value less a **holding-company discount**, and the unlisted subsidiaries at cost or investment value. MOSL, the broker with the most regular notes, uses exactly this (FY28E standalone at 15x, listed subsidiaries at a 35% discount, target ₹3,379, Aug-2026). A P/E on consolidated EPS is not how the stock is priced: CG Power's earnings are in it at TII's multiple rather than at CG Power's own (~106x trailing), and TICMPL's losses at 100%.

blocks.h: The holding-company discount: derived from TII's own history

blocks.p: House method (as in our Godrej Industries report): at every quarter-end since June 2021 we compare TII's market value with the value of what it owns, on the same conventions as our SOTP: the standalone business at 19x the next year's core EPS (actual, our estimates for FY27-28), the unlisted subsidiaries at TII's cost, and CG Power and Shanthi Gears at that day's market price (TII's shares held from the annual reports). What is left of TII's market value after the standalone business and the unlisted subsidiaries is what the market pays for the listed stakes; the **discount** is how far that falls short of their market value.

blocks.p: **Judging the median against today.** The history has two regimes. From 2021 to mid-2024 TII traded at a *premium* to this look-through value (median -16.0% over all 21 quarters): the market paid for the CG Power turnaround, the EV story and the Murugappa team's record before CG Power's own price caught up. Since September 2024 CG Power has kept rising while TII fell, and the discount has stayed between 7.7% and 52.2% (median 34.0%). On 30-Sep-2026 it was **64.7%**, the widest ever: TII's whole market value was ₹45,969 cr against ₹75,724 cr for its CG Power shares alone. **There is no dated structural break at Sep-2024.** We looked for one: the CG Power holding reached its current 88.65 cr shares in Mar-2023, TICMPL's last outside round was signed in May-2024, CG Power's QIP was in Jul-Sep 2025 and the look-through conventions do not change in between. Sep-2024 is simply the first quarter-end at which TII traded below its look-through value, and the same two-year window we used for Godrej Industries. So our **base-case 34% is a judgement against the as-of level**, not a mechanical application of the rule: the full-window median (-16.0%) implies a premium to look-through value, which we do not assume for a holding company that has never sold a CG Power share and keeps funding loss-making ventures, while today's 65% is the widest ever. 34% is close to MOSL's 35%. The bear case keeps today's 65%; the bull case uses the full-window median floored at zero, which is also our judgement (no premium). segments.name: CG Power (100%)
segments._why: Motors, drives, railway equipment (industrial systems), transformers and switchgear (power systems), and the new semiconductor businesses (CG Semi OSAT, Axiro). Revenue +25% in FY26, +14% in Q1FY27 (power systems +31%). New EHV switchgear plant from Jun-2026; CG Semi's G1 OSAT plant in production from Jul-2026. 15% / 16% / 15%. Consolidated for the P&L only: in the valuation TII's 56.29% is at market. CG Power is covered separately; we take no view on its own valuation here.
segments._marginWhy: Screener EBITDA margin 13.2% FY26, 12.1% Q1FY27 as semiconductor start-up losses rose (segment loss Rs50 cr vs Rs9 cr). 12.5% / 13.2% / 13.6% as OSAT volumes ramp.

segments.name: Shanthi Gears (100%)
segments._why: Industrial gears and gearboxes (steel, cement, power, sugar). Revenue fell 14% in FY26 and 15% in Q1FY27 (Rs115 cr). FY27E -5% (weak H1, recovery in H2 on ~Rs100 cr of capex), then +12% a year.

segments.name: EV and new ventures (residual)
segments._why: Consolidated less standalone, CG Power and Shanthi Gears: TI Clean Mobility (EV segment revenue Rs683 cr FY26, Rs239 cr in Q1FY27, +77%), TI Medical (~20% growth guided), 3xper, Kcaltech, Sedis, less eliminations. Residual revenue Rs453 cr in Q1FY27 (+57%). +40% / +35% / +30%.
segments._marginWhy: Residual EBITDA -Rs538 cr FY25, -Rs550 cr FY26 (-41%), about -24% in Q1FY27 (EV segment loss Rs147 cr). Management: past peak quarterly losses, one EV business to break even in FY27 and two more in FY28. -24% / -15% / -8%: losses narrow but do not end in our forecast.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any block (inside the residual)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Eliminations and unallocated items are inside the residual block, defined so that the four blocks sum to reported consolidated revenue and EBITDA.
assumptions._capexWhy: Consolidated capex (Screener: FY24 Rs851 cr, FY25 Rs1,213 cr, FY26 Rs1,433 cr). FY27 guidance: TII ~Rs350 cr, Shanthi Gears ~Rs100 cr, group excluding CG Power Rs600-700 cr. CG Power's own capex (switchgear, transformers, CG Semi's OSAT plant) is not guided in our sources (gap): we assume ~Rs1,100 cr in FY27E, falling as the OSAT phase-1 spend ends.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs664 cr = 7.7% of average gross block; Q1FY27 Rs183 cr (Rs732 cr annualised). 7.2% gives ~Rs745 cr in FY27E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Other income is entered as a build (below), not as a yield on the consolidated cash, because most of the cash sits in CG Power.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener other income before exceptional items ('other income normal'): FY25 Rs371 cr, FY26 Rs387 cr, TTM Jun-26 Rs447 cr (Q1FY27 Rs112 cr). Mostly CG Power's treasury income (Rs208 cr FY26, Rs84 cr in Q1FY27 after its QIP) plus TII's non-dividend other income (~Rs69 cr: grants, rent, MF gains) and Shanthi Gears (~Rs15 cr). TII's dividends from CG Power and Shanthi Gears cancel out on consolidation. Rs450 / 480 / 510 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs79 cr (incl. ~Rs29 cr on leases), Q1FY27 Rs16 cr. Group gross debt Rs754 cr at Mar-26.
assumptions._taxWhy: The tax line also carries minorities (engine workaround, as in GODREJIND and UPL): 43.71% of CG Power's and 29.54% of Shanthi Gears' profits belong to other shareholders, and TICMPL's losses carry no tax credit. FY26: tax Rs734 cr + minorities Rs481 cr = 66% of PBT (Rs1,852 cr); FY25 59%. Our parts build (TII 25.2%, CG 26%, Shanthi 25%, residual untaxed) gives 62.5% / 58% / 55% as the untaxed losses shrink relative to profits.

saBuild._why: TII standalone profit before its dividends from CG Power and Shanthi Gears (they are valued at market, so their dividends must not be capitalised again in the P/E part). FY26 standalone: depreciation Rs188 cr (PBDIT 1,295 less PBIT 1,107), other income Rs211 cr of which Rs142 cr dividends from subsidiaries, interest ~Rs8 cr, tax 23.6% (statutory 25.17%). Core PAT FY26 = 821 - 142.27 x (1 - 25.17%) = Rs715 cr. Depreciation rises with ~Rs350 cr a year of capex; non-dividend other income Rs70-80 cr.

assumptions._payoutWhy: TII has paid Rs3.50 a share every year since FY21 (~Rs68 cr, ~8-11% of attributable profit).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Steel costs are fully passed through and engineering volumes keep growing in double digits; CG Power grows ~20% with semiconductor losses fading fast; TICMPL breaks even on schedule and is worth what outside investors paid; the holding-company discount returns to its 2021-26 median.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Price resets lag again and margins stay near the Q1FY27 level; auto and industrial demand slows; CG Power's semiconductor ramp drags; TICMPL needs the full Rs750 cr programme and its equity is worth nothing; the discount stays as wide as on 30-Sep-2026.

parts.name: TII standalone businesses: P/E on Sep-28E core EPS
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E core profit (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E, before CG/Shanthi dividends) ₹917 cr × 19x (bull 21x on ₹1,026 cr, bear 15.5x on ₹770 cr)
parts.note: TII's own one-year-forward P/E while the share was the standalone business only (listing to Mar-2020): median 20.8x, cut by the 9.4% auto-component de-rating at 30-Sep-2026.

parts.name: Less: holding-company discount on the listed stakes
parts.metricLabel: Discount × listed stakes ₹78,858 cr (base 34%, bull 0%, bear 65%)
parts.note: Derived from TII's own discount at 21 quarter-ends since Jun-2021 (see Valuation).

parts.name: TI Clean Mobility: TII's investment
parts.metricLabel: Base: TII's cost ₹1,000 cr; bull: Mar-26 fair-value mark ₹1,576 cr; bear: equity worth nothing and the remaining ₹500 cr of the ₹750 cr programme lost (PV ₹473 cr)
parts.note: Outside investors (~₹1,780 cr) hold CCPS that convert only at an IPO; their stake was marked at ₹2,404.70 cr in Mar-2026.

parts.name: Other unlisted subsidiaries at cost
parts.metricLabel: TI Medical ₹265 cr, 3xper ₹310 cr, Kcaltech ₹62 cr, Financière C10 (Sedis) ₹61 cr
parts.note: At TII's cost (AR FY26 note 6a; Q1FY27 deck).

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values TII (Motilal Oswal: standalone on P/E, listed subsidiaries at a holding-company discount): ~85% of the look-through value is the market value of CG Power and Shanthi Gears.

methods.name: P/E on consolidated EPS
methods.why: Own one-year-forward P/E on consolidated EPS since Apr-2021: median 62.3x (no trough years), cut by the 9.4% sector de-rating: 56.5x. Rough: consolidated EPS carries CG Power at earnings, not at its ~100x market multiple, and TICMPL's losses at 100%.
